title: AO/517/2015 of YOGESH TOMAR Vs SMT. KAMLESH

paras.text:
IN HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Appeal From Order No.517 of 2015
Yogesh Tomar .....Appellant
Vs.
Smt. Kamlesh & others ...Respondents
Advocate: Mr. Narendra Bali, Advocate for the appellant.
 Mr. Vikas Bahuguna, Advocate for the claimants.
 Mr. V.K. Kohli, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Kanti Ram Sharma, Advocate for
 respondent no.3.

Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
The appellant before this Court, in the present an appeal from order
is the owner of the offending vehicle, that is a tractor trolley, bearing
Registration No.U.A. 08G 9635 and the trolley was bearing the Registration No.
U.A. 08G 9636. It is contended that when the tractor trolley was engaged in
carrying mine and minerals, on the date of the accident i.e. on 08.03.2014, the
deceased Murari Lal Saini, admittedly according to the claimants pleadings was
travelling on the offending vehicle, but on account of some technical fault, the
wheel of the tractor gave way due to which the driver of the tractor lost its
control and the deceased who was sitting on the vehicle met with an accident,
and as a consequence of the injuries suffered by him, he died.
2. The claimants, who were the dependent of deceased Murari Lal had
file their claim petition on 11.07.2014, before the Motor Accident Claim
Tribunal and according to the claimants, they have submitted in their pleadings
that on the date of accident Murari Lal was travelling on the vehicle. The matter
proceeded. The notices were issued to the respective parties to the proceedings
of M.A.C.P. No.75 of 2014, Smt. Kamlesh and another vs. Yogesh Tomar and
another, and in support of their contention, the claimant had submitted, that the
accident had chanced on account of rash and negligent driving of the tractor by
opposite party no.2 i.e. Karan, the driver of the tractor and due to which the
death has taken place of Murari Lal, who on the date of the death was of 45
years of age and was alleged to be working as a labourer on the tractor trolley
and was being paid with Rs.300/- per day as a labour charges and consequently

2
it has also been contended, that he was earning about Rs.8,000/-per month.
Thus, determining the total liability, which was claimed by the claimants in the
claim petition, they have claimed for the relief of remittance of a total amount of
Rs.27,25,000/- including various other expenditures, which were incurred into
for meeting up the funeral expenses and for love and affection etc.
3. The defendants had put in appearance and had filed their written
statement. Defendent nos.1 & 2, have filed their written statement being Paper
No.20-B, wherein in the statement thus recorded by defendant no.1 & 2, they
have admitted the fact of the occurrence of the accident on 08.03.2014, but
however the opposite party no.2 to the claim proceedings, had denied in their
pleading the fact that the deceased was travelling on the offending vehicle,
rather opposite party no.2 has submitted, that he was driving the tractor and he
was seated on the driver seat and since there was no other space available and
permissible in the vehicle to enable any other person to travel on the same, it
cannot be accepted that the deceased was sitting on the sitting and rather tried to
avoid their liability of remittance of the compensation to be paid to the
dependent of the deceased by raising a plea to that effect that in order to bring
the accident within the ambit of the insurance policy that the vehicle was insured
under policy with one seating capacity, the deceased would be treated to be the
gratuitous passenger.
4. The Insurance Company that is opposite party no.3, had filed their
independent written statement i.e. being Paper No.19-B and had submitted that
as far as the tractor is concerned, it was though validly insured with the
Insurance Company, but they denied their liability for the purposes of remittance
of the amount of claimed compensation, for the reason being that the deceased
was a gratuitous passenger, who was permitted to travel on the vehicle by the
driver of the vehicle, where he was employed as a labourer and being a
gratuitous passenger, that itself was in contravention to the terms of the
Insurance policy, the Insurance Company denied their liability to pay the
compensation as claimed by the claimants in the Claim Petition which filed by
them before the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal.

3
5. The Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, has framed as many as six
issues vide it's order of 01.08.2014, which are extracted hereunder:-

6. The claimants in support of their contention had presented
themselves in the witness box and recorded their witnesses in examination-in-chief by way of evidence Paper No.33-B and 3-B, apart from it, also producing
the witness of P.W.1 and P.W.2. These witnesses produced by the claimants
were also cross examined by the opposite parties to the proceedings. The owner
of the vehicle in support of his contention had placed on record the documents
by way of list Paper No.22-Ga, pertaining to the registration of the tractor and
the trolley and the fitness certificate, the permit, which was granted to the
vehicle, the license, the Insurance Policy and receipts of taxes, which were
deposited by them by way of at list Paper No.23-Ga and 30-Ga .
7. The learned trial court while dealing with the issues thus framed for
the purposes of fixation of liability for the payment of the compensation
depending upon peculiar circumstances of the case, where the deceased was
travelling on the vehicle itself, as it was contended by the claimants, who was
employed as a labourer on the offending vehicle, in fact it was a fact which was
attempted to be denied by the owner of the vehicle, contending to the contrary
thereof that in fact, the deceased was rather not travelling on the vehicle, but was
rather standing by the side to the road when the rear wheel of the vehicle gave
way and due to which the rear bigger wheel of the tractor went off the vehicle
and hit the deceased due to which he met with the sad demise.

4
8. The counsel the appellant had submitted, that if the statement of
witnesses which were recorded before the court below and particularly that of
the D.W.2 is concerned is taken into consideration, it is an admitted case that
Mr. Yogesh Tomar, was the driver of the vehicle and he had recorded his
statement to the effect that the accident occurred due to the technical flaw in the
axel of the vehicle by virtue of which the right rear wheel of the tractor has gone
off, the vehicle resulting into an accident. But what is important to be considered
is that if the statement of the driver of the vehicle is taken into consideration in
its totality, when he has tried to project fact that the deceased was standing by
the side of the road, when the wheel of the tractor hit him resulting into to his
death, in fact in para 3 of the written statement, he has rather submitted that he
was not knowing Mr. Murari Lal, but simultaneously in the same paragraph he
has submitted to the contrary that he was not knowing Mr. Murari Lal, because
of the fact that he was employed with the owner of the vehicle just two or three
days before the accident. In that eventuality if the rightful interpretation is given
to the statement recorded in para 3 and on a harmonious construction of it, sit
could be reasonably inferred that in fact Murari Lal, was actually employed with
the owner of the vehicle as a labourer of the offending vehicle and he was not
aware and not known to D.W.-2, because he himself was employed by the
owner of the offending vehicle only, couple of days, earlier. Hence, the stand
and the argument which was extended by the counsel for the appellant, that the
deceased was not employed and was not travelling on the vehicle, cannot be
accepted for the reason being that the claimants themselves have submitted that
the deceased was travelling on the vehicle and that even stands fortified by the
statement of the witnesses recorded by them before the court below.
9. In fact, if the written statement of the Insurance Company is taken
into consideration and the documents too which were produced by opposite
party no.1 & 2, the Insurance policy cover itself shows that the vehicle though it
stood insured with the Insurance Company on the date of accident, but the same
was being driven in contravention to the terms and conditions of the Insurance
policy itself, because the permitted number of persons, who could travel on the
vehicle was only one, that is the driver itself and no other individual could be
permitted to travel on the vehicle contrary to the provisions of the Insurance
policy and hence for all practical purposes the deceased would be falling within

5
the ambit of being a gratuitous passenger and if that be the condition and in that
eventuality the Insurance Company contended that they would not be liable to
pay any compensation since the deceased would not be a person, who would be
covered under the Insurance policy of the offending vehicle.
10. On the basis of the aforesaid appreciation of facts and evidence
which were placed before the Court, the learned Motor Accident Claim Tribunal
in its para 36 of the award had considered the parameters for fixation of liability
on appreciating the contents of the Insurance policy and had ultimately arrived
to a conclusion, that since the deceased was a gratuitous passenger, who was
permitted to sit and travel on the tractor beyond the permissible laden capacity,
in fact, it would be the owner of the vehicle, who would be liable to pay the
compensation and thus the determination made of assessing the compensation
payable to the claimant to the tune of Rs.7,10,000/- along with the interest at the
rate of 6%, which has been levied upon the owner of the vehicle is absolutely
justified and in consonance to the ratio, which has been relief by the counsel for
the respondents Insurance Company as reported in (2015) (3) ALJ 347
National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Smt. Leela alias Vimla and
particularly reference has been made to para 8, 14 and 19 of the aforesaid
judgment, as it has been rendered by the court, wherein it has been observed,
that the tractor which has a insurance cover of only one sitting capacity and if
the deceased labourer was found to be travelling on the vehicle, he would not
fall to be covered by the Insurance policy and the terms contained in it, and it
would rather the owner who would be liable and not the Insurance company.
Paragraph 8, 14 & 19 are extracted hereunder:-
"8. The Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation in
the present case to the claimants as the tractor is not constructed to
carry any load other than equipment used for the purpose of
propulsion and excludes the road-roller, so once it is established
from the report that Sri Ishwardeen (deceased) a passenger
travelling on the tractor, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay
any compensation rather is payable by the owner of the vehicle. In
support of his contention, he has placed reliance on the judgment
given by Himachal Pradesh High Court in the case of New India
Assurance Company Ltd. v. Sudesh Kumari and others, 2007 (3)
TAC 895 (H.P.), Mohan Kushwaha and others v. Ghanshyam and
another, 2012 (3) TAC) 299 (All), Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Anil Kumar and others, 2013 (2) TAC 298 (P & H.), as well as on
the judgment given by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of New

6
India Assurance company Ltd. v. Vedwati and others, 2007 AICC
635. So, the judgment passed by the Tribunal being contrary to law,
liable to be set aside.
14. Accordingly, the question which is to be considered in the
present case is whether the Insurance Company is liable to pay any
compensation is the claimant due to death of Sri Ishwardeen who
was travelling on a tractor for agricultural work. The tractor is
defined under Section 2(44) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 and it
is specifically provides that it is not constructed to carry any load
other than equipment used for the purpose of propulsion and
excludes the road-roller. The insurance is for death or bodily injury
by an accident by the use of motor vehicle which in this case is
tractor. The consideration would, therefore, be whether a person
travelling/sitting on the tractor is entitled to any cover for insurance
against the Insurance Company. Hon'ble the Apex Court in the case
of New India Assurance company Ltd. v. Vedwati and others, 2007
AICC 635: (2007 (3) ALJ 193), held as under:
"On a closer reading of the expressions "goods vehicle", "public
service vehicle", "state carrier" and "transport vehicle" occurring in
Sections 2(8), 2(25), 2(29) and 2(33) of the old Act with the
corresponding provisions i.e. Section 2(14), 2(35), 2(40) and 2(47)
of the Act, it is clear that there are conceptual differences. The
provisions read as follows: Old Act:
"2(8) "goods vehicle" means any motor vehicle constructed or
adapted for use for the carriage of goods, or any motor vehicle not
so constructed or adapted when used for the carriage of goods
solely or in addition to passengers"
"2(25) "public service vehicle" means any motor vehicle used or
adapted to be used for the carriage of passengers for hire or reward
and includes a motor cab contract carriage, and stage carriage."
"2(29) "stage carriage" means a motor vehicle carrying or adapted
to carry more than six persons excluding the driver which carries
passengers for hire or reward at separate fares paid by or for
individual passengers either for the whole journey or for stages of
the journey:" "2(33) "transport vehicle" means a public service
vehicle or a goods vehicle:"
The Act (New Act):
"2(14) "goods carriage" any motor vehicle constructed or adapted
for use solely for the carriage of goods or any motor vehicle not to
constructed or adapted when used for the carriage of goods:"
"2(35) "public service vehicles" means any motor vehicles used or
adapted to be used for the carriage of passengers for hire or reward,
and includes a maxi cab a motor cab, contract and stage carriage:"

7
"2(40) "stage carriage" means a motor vehicle constructed or
adapted to carry more than six passengers excluding the driver for
(SIC) or reward at separate fares paid by or for individual
passengers either for the whole journey or for stages of the
journey:" "2(47) "transport vehicle" means a public services vehicle
a goods carriage an educational institution bus or a private service
vehicle:"
(Underlined for emphasis)
"Liability" as defined in Section 145(c) of the Act reads as follows:
"Liability", wherever used in relation to the death of or bodily
injury to any person, includes liability in respect thereof under
Section 140."
Third party risks in the background of vehicles which are
subject-matter of insurance are dealt with in Chapter VIII of the old
Act and Chapter XI of the Act. Proviso to Section 147 of the Act
(sic) is to be (sic) with Section 96 of the old Act. Proviso to Section
147 of the Act reads as follows: 'Provided that a policy shall not be
required
(i) to cover liability in respect of the death arising out of and
in the course of his employment of the employee of a person
insured by the policy or in respect of bodily injure sustained by
such an employee arising out of and in the course of his
employment other than a liability arising under the Workmen's
Compensation Act, 1993 (8 of 1923) in respect of the death of or
bodily injury to, any such employee-
(a) engaged in driving the vehicle, or
(b) if it is a public service vehicle engaged as conductor of the
vehicle or in examining tickets on the vehicles, or
(c) if it is a good carriage, being carried in the vehicle, or
(ii) to cover any contractual liability."
It is of significance that proviso appended to Section 95 of
the old Act contained Clause (ii) which does not find place in the
Act. The same reads as follows:-
"except where the vehicle is a vehicle in which passengers
are carried for hire or reward or by reason of or in pursuance of a
contract of employment to cover liability in respect of the death of
or bodily injury to persons being carried in or upon or entering or
mounting or alighting from the vehicle at the time of the occurrence
of the event out of which a claim arises."
The difference in the language of "goods vehicle" as appear
in the old Act and "goods carriage" in the Act is of significance. A
bare reading of the provisions makes it clear that the legislative
intent was to prohibit goods vehicle from carrying any passenger.
This is clear from the expression "in addition to passengers" as
contained in definition of "good vehicle" in the old Act. The
position becomes further clear because the expression used is "good
carriage" is solely for the carriage of goods. Carrying of passengers
in a goods carriage is not contemplated in the Act. There is no
provision similar to Clause (ii) of the proviso appended to Section
95 of the old Act prescribing requirement of insurance policy. Even
Section 147 of the Act mandates compulsory coverage against
death of or bodily injury to any passenger of "public service

8
vehicle". The proviso makes it further clear that compulsory
coverage in respect of drivers and conductors of public service
vehicle and employees carried in goods vehicle would be limited to
liability under the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 (in short
WC Act"). There is no reference to any passenger in "goods
carriage".
The inevitable conclusion, therefore, is that provisions of the
Act do not enjoin any statutory liability on the owner of a vehicle to
get his vehicle insured for any passenger travelling in a goods
carriage and the insurer would have no liability therefore.
Our view gets support from a recent decision of a three-Judge Bench of this Court in New India Assurance Company
Limited v. Asha Rani and others, 2002 (8) Supreme 594, in which it
has been held that Satpal Singh's case (supra) was not correctly
decided. That being the position, the Tribunal and the High Court
were not justified in holding that the insurer had the liability to
satisfy the award. This position was also highlighted in Oriental
Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Devireddy Konda Reddy and others, 2003 (2)
SCC 339. Subsequently also in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Ajit
Kumar and others, 2003 (9) SCC 668, in National Insurance Co.
Ltd. v. Baljit Kaur and others, 2004 (2) SCC 1 and in National
Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Bommithi Subbhayamma and others, 2005
(12) SCC 243, the view in Asha Rani's case (supra) was reiterated.
Above being the position, the impugned order of the High
Court is not sustainable and we accordingly set aside the same.
19. For the foregoing reasons, the appeal filed by the National
Insurance Company Ltd. is allowed and the judgment and award
dated 9.3.2009 passed by the Motor Accident Claim
Tribunal/Additional District Judge, Court No. 7, Barabani in
M.A.C.P. No. 129 of 2001 (Smt. Leela Alias Vimal and others v.
National Insurance Company Ltd. and others) thereby awarding a
sum of Rs. 1,67,599/- with 6% interest from the date of
presentation of the claim petition is modified to the extent that the
National Insurance Company Ltd./appellant is not liable to pay the
same rather to be recovered from the owner of the tractor having
registration No. U.P. 41B 3073 i.e. from Sri Sanjay Kumar Gupta
and the said amount should be paid by him within a period of three
months from today to the claimants."
11. In view of the aforesaid reasoning and the aspect already dealt with
that since the deceased labourer who was sitting on the vehicle was not covered
under the Insurance policy and the tractor itself was being driven on the date of
accident in contravention to the terms of the Insurance company, the liability of
paying the compensation has been rightly fasten upon the owner of the vehicle.
Apart from the above argument, no other argument has been raised by the

9
counsel for the appellant. Hence the appeal lacks merit and the same is
accordingly, dismissed.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 31.03.2022
